description: We are a motivated team passionate about space, science, and technology. We love creating ideas, solving problems, and learning together. We are looking for creative, responsible, and enthusiastic teammates with skills in coding, design, research, or communication. Join us and let’s explore beyond together!
summary: What happens to a rover after its final drive? We created an illustrated story for students about the equipment NASA missions left on the Moon and Mars. Using NASA photographs and mission records, we follow the Apollo 15 astronauts as they park their lunar rover and learn how instruments they left behind kept recording moonquakes after they returned to Earth. On Mars, we tell the story of Opportunity, a rover built for 90 Martian days that explored for almost 15 years. We also show why engineers wanted a closer look at Perseverance’s parachute after landing. Through these stories, students discover how objects left behind preserve the history of exploration and help engineers plan future missions.
details:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an illustrated story for school-age readers. It begins with a question: If you were an astronaut about to leave the Moon, what would you leave behind? Each chapter follows a real object and explains what it did, why it stayed, and what we can still learn from it.

On the Moon, readers follow the Apollo 15 astronauts as they park their electric rover for the last time. Nearby, instruments they set up keep recording moonquakes for years after the crew returns home. On Mars, readers discover how Opportunity, a rover designed to work for 90 Martian days, found evidence of ancient water. The final chapter looks at Perseverance’s parachute through the camera of the Ingenuity helicopter. A photograph taken more than a year after landing gave engineers a chance to study how the landing equipment performed.

We used NASA mission histories and photographs to build each chapter around a specific moment. We chose short sentences and explained technical terms so students could follow the story without already knowing how a space mission works. Our goal is for readers to look at a photograph of a parked rover or a fallen parachute and ask their own scientific questions about what they see.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI)

We used ChatGPT to help draft the English text for the Moon and Mars chapters, organize the mission information into a story for students, and simplify technical explanations. We also used ChatGPT to draft the project summary and project details for this submission. The mission information and photographs referenced in the story come from NASA.
